skill.name: go-public
skill.description: Convert an AI prompt workflow into a public web page with visitor inputs, sequential AI steps, and results. Validate, test, build, publish, update, or delete pages through a Python helper.
skill.summary: Publish reusable AI workflows as public forms through OneTag, without visitor accounts or personal API keys.
skill.author: fengyiqicoder

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown, CSS, DOM access, or expected publishing operations, not command execution or reconnaissance. Confirmed risks involve edit-token file permissions, an unpinned remote script, incomplete Git exclusion, and unsafe placeholder replacement. No evidence found of malicious intent, covert exfiltration, or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: The private edit token is written before its file receives restrictive permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Create the state file with mode 0600 before writing credentials, reject symlinks, and use atomic replacement for existing state.

remediation.issue: Generated pages execute a mutable third-party SDK without an integrity check.
remediation.suggestion: Use an immutable SDK release with subresource integrity where supported, and document the external script's access to page inputs.

remediation.issue: Automatic credential exclusion only runs when the current folder contains a .git directory.
remediation.suggestion: Handle nested repository folders and worktrees, verify the state file is ignored, and warn users when exclusion cannot be established.

remediation.issue: Title replacement modifies workflow strings after JavaScript-safe serialization.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the HTML title before inserting serialized workflow data, or use a template API that never reprocesses inserted values.

semantic_findings.title: Incomplete Git exclusion can expose page-management credentials
semantic_findings.description: Credential exclusion runs only when the current directory contains a .git directory. Nested repository folders and worktrees can leave the edit-token file eligible for accidental commits.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guard checks only a local .git directory, while documentation promises repository exclusion. Worktrees use a .git file; nested directories lack that entry.

semantic_findings.title: Post-serialization placeholder replacement enables script injection
semantic_findings.description: Replacing __TITLE__ after workflow serialization also replaces matching text inside workflow strings. A crafted title can introduce executable JavaScript into those strings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: An isolated reproduction of the replacement order executed an injected expression inside a workflow value. Only ampersands and less-than signs are escaped in the replacement title.

content.user_title: Publish AI Workflows as Public Web Tools
content.value_statement: Useful AI workflows are difficult to share with people who lack accounts or API keys. This skill builds and publishes reusable input forms through OneTag.
actual_capabilities: Validate workflow titles, field types, step identifiers, variable references, and visible results.
Run example inputs through the OneTag AI API and print each step's result.
Generate a single HTML file with text fields, text areas, selection lists, and clickable examples.
Chain AI steps using earlier answers and stream the last visible result in the browser.
Publish or update a page through OneTag and retain its management credentials locally.
Delete the published page using its saved edit token.
limitations: AI execution and hosting depend on OneTag; service availability and backend security were not verified in this source review.
Published pages use service-controlled daily allowances and visitor rate limits.
Pages have no application login, payment processing, database, or persistent visitor storage.
Workflow prompts, hidden steps, and examples are embedded in public HTML; hidden results do not make instructions confidential.

use_cases.title: Share a meeting follow-up tool
use_cases.description: Turn a tested notes-to-email workflow into a public form that extracts decisions and drafts a follow-up message.

use_cases.title: Publish a writing exercise
use_cases.description: Offer learners a form that transforms sample text through sequential feedback and revision prompts.

use_cases.title: Distribute a reusable client tool
use_cases.description: Publish a non-sensitive brief-to-outline workflow with example inputs, then update its prompts without changing the shared link.

prompt_templates.title: Define a simple workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn our last prompt into a public tool. Show the visitor inputs, AI steps, visible results, and title for my confirmation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: define the tool before building.

prompt_templates.title: Build and test a page
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the confirmed workflow with fictional examples. Validate it, run one example through OneTag, and show the result before publishing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: verify behavior using a real AI response.

prompt_templates.title: Publish sequential prompts
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a two-step notes-to-email tool with a tone selector. Keep extraction intermediate, show the final email, and explain public prompt visibility.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: connect inputs and intermediate answers.

prompt_templates.title: Update an existing public tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing workflow and preserve its saved page state. Retest revised prompts, rebuild, and update the same link after my approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: maintain a published tool without exposing management credentials.

output_examples.input: Turn this fictional meeting into decisions and an email: The launch moves to December 2. Alex owns testing by Friday.
output: What was decided: The launch moves to December 2.
Action item: Alex completes testing by Friday.
Follow-up email: Team, the launch is now December 2. Alex will complete testing by Friday.

output_examples.input: Publish the validated notes-to-email workflow after I approve its example output.
output: The helper prints the published page link and the service-reported limits.
The private edit token is saved locally in .go-public.json for updates and deletion.
Visitors can enter notes, choose a tone, and receive the configured plain-text results.

best_practices: Use fictional examples and remove confidential instructions, because published HTML includes the complete workflow.
Review example output and the external service's data policies before sending sensitive inputs or approving publication.
Keep .go-public.json private, verify its permissions and Git exclusion, and retain it for later updates or deletion.
anti_patterns: Do not publish passwords, payment details, private conversation data, or impersonation forms.
Do not treat hidden steps or system prompts as secrets when their workflow is embedded in the public page.
Do not promise unlimited usage or use this form-based tool as a replacement for authenticated applications.

faq.question: Do visitors need an account or their own API key?
faq.answer: The documented flow uses a page-specific OneTag allowance, so visitors do not provide personal accounts or API keys.

faq.question: Which inputs and workflow structures are supported?
faq.answer: Forms support text areas, single-line fields, and selection lists. Sequential AI steps can reference visitor inputs and earlier answers.

faq.question: Where do AI requests and published pages go?
faq.answer: The helper defaults to onetagai.com for testing and publishing. Generated pages load the OneTag SDK and use it for AI requests.

faq.question: Can I update or delete a published page?
faq.answer: Keep .go-public.json private in the same folder. Rebuild and publish to update the link, or use the helper's delete command.

faq.question: What happens when the free allowance runs out?
faq.answer: The page displays a quota message. The skill documents daily resets and optional page claiming for account-based allowances.

faq.question: Are prompts and hidden steps private?
faq.answer: No. The generated HTML embeds the complete workflow, including prompts, examples, and hidden steps. Do not include confidential material.
